result:
Round 248 **passes**. Snap now pauses when the grid lines are too dense to draw, and I checked this in a real browser at 1440×900 and 1280×720. I compared the round's code (`:5173`) against an unchanged copy of the previous commit running alongside (`:5174`). No app files were changed during my check.

**What I measured:**
- **Hidden grid:** I tested three hidden-grid setups: 0.1 s at 40 px/s, the adaptive grid at the widest zoom-out, and 1/32 after adding the pulse stem. A ruler click, a click on an empty lane, a playhead drag and a clip drag all landed where the pointer was. The previous commit snapped to the invisible line (for example 8.487 vs 8.5, and 669.56 vs 670). Library drops behave the same way (3.125 vs 3.100).
- **Alt over a hidden grid:** Alt no longer switches the grid on, with Snap on or off. With the lines visible, Alt + Snap off still snaps (10.696 → 10.7), as before.
- **Visible grids are unchanged:** every value equals the previous commit, including the loop brace and marker drags. The 1/32-at-100 px/s click at 1280 that A and B couldn't measure cleanly is now valid.
- **Zooming back in** resumes snapping without any key press. `data-snap-paused` flips from true to false, and the Snap button stays pressed throughout.
- **Arrow keys:** a selected clip moves 0 → 0.1 → 0.2 → 0.25 (the previous commit jumped 0.25 → 0.5 → 0.75). Markers and the loop move 0.1 s while the lines are hidden, then to the next grid line once visible.
- **Signals:** the "Snap is paused" note and tooltips appear after every one of the six grid actions, including adaptive `3` (1/8T) and the grid-menu width items. There is no note when the result is visible or Snap is off. The longest note still fits on one line at both widths.
- **Standing checks:** export and playback work and the export WAV matches the expected hash (16.000 s). The screen text count is unchanged. Anonymous access to `/studio-lab` works, and the premium route still requires sign-in (`/api/studio-token` returns 401 with no credentials).
- **Unit tests:** the 134 covering test files pass (2,073 tests). All 10 mutation runs failed exactly the tests B predicted.

**Ableton comparison:** snapping to visible lines and Alt with the grid off both match the manual. Alt over a hidden grid is a deliberate difference, and snapping while the lines are hidden has no Live reference, so it stays unconfirmed. Saba's question on this (SABA-Q-11B-HIDDEN-SNAP) is still open.

**Findings for B:**
- **C-R248-01 (Low):** doc 186 is marked "Completed" but contradicts what shipped. Its title still says stages 1 and 2a only. Lines 186–188 say every gesture still reads the old grid value, which is no longer true. Both are outside A's allowed edits.
- **Info:** after zooming in, the status still says Snap is paused. After zooming out, it says plain "Snap on" while paused. The task rules this as intended, and it is part of Saba's question.
- **Info, existing behaviour:** in adaptive mode at 120 BPM, `3` on 1/4 gives 1/8T. A Snap off + Alt clip drag on a visible grid can keep an off-grid start. Both behave the same in the previous commit.
- **Not verified:** snapping on the purchased-product route needs the backend, which isn't available in the cloud, so it is marked blocked. The full test suite and build are for the root gate.

Everything is in `/home/runner/czaba-project/tmp/studio-real-loop`:

- c-round-248.json (`browserVerified`: true)
- c-round-248/ (scripts, measurements and screenshots)
